answers.core: Because `Node` is the most fundamental part of the engine.
answers.workaround:
There's hardly a way to override the "Create Root Node" form.

There are currently several ways to workaround this:

1. You have to click "Custom Node" just to instantiate a scene inheriting from `Node`.

2. Adding `Node` to a list of favorites, and clicking on the "Star" to display that. The problem with this approach is that I have to re-add other built-in nodes (`Node2D`, `Control` etc) to the list to make it look like the default one without having to switch between favorites and defaults.

3. Navigate with the mouse to `New Scene`, proceed with keyboard with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> → <kbd>Enter</kbd> https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/1206#issuecomment-659807343.

To summarize, you have to use both the mouse and the keyboard in all those cases (which is known to be slow for developers), and that's a lot of steps just to create a scene with a root `Node`, and even if something can be tweaked, it's tiresome to do this process throughout other projects and/or machines.

Related usability proposal: #679.

title: Add the `Node` as an option in "Create Root Node" to create plain scenes
